stories.title: Media Outlets Return to White House Following Court Order, Denied Access to State Dinner
stories.summary: Several media outlets, including CNN and MS NOW, returned to the White House after a judge ordered the restoration of their press passes, which had been revoked by the Trump administration. However, reporters from these outlets were denied access to cover the arrival of Chinese leader Xi Jinping at a state dinner, despite the court ruling.

stories.title: Supreme Court Allows Trump Administration to Use Federal Voter Eligibility Database Temporarily
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has temporarily lifted restrictions on a federal voter eligibility database, allowing the Trump administration to use it ahead of the upcoming elections. This decision, made in a 6-3 ruling, supports the administration's efforts to verify voter citizenship status and potentially purge noncitizens from voter rolls. Critics have raised concerns about privacy and the implications of such actions on voter access.

stories.title: Shooting Victim from 2024 Trump Rally in Butler Passes Away
stories.summary: James Copenhaver, 76, who was shot during an assassination attempt at a Trump campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, has died from complications related to his injuries. The shooting also resulted in the death of another individual and grazed Trump's ear with a bullet. Trump expressed his condolences, calling Copenhaver's death a 'tremendous loss.'

stories.title: Netanyahu Criticizes UN Delegates Who Walked Out During His Speech

stories.title: Renewed Fighting Erupts in Northern Ethiopia as Tigray Rebels Declare War
stories.summary: Fighting has intensified in northern Ethiopia as Tigray's rebel authorities declare a 'full-blown war' against the Ethiopian government. The Ethiopian army reports that 272 Tigrayan fighters have been killed and 260 wounded during a counter-offensive in the Amhara region, although these figures have not been independently verified. The conflict is also spreading into neighboring regions, raising concerns of a potential humanitarian crisis similar to the previous civil war.
